summary:
Graviton (ARM) CPU inference routing is implemented for PyTorch and TensorFlow; nothing is committed.

Changes:
- src/sagemaker/fw_utils.py: added GRAVITON_ALLOWED_TARGET_INSTANCE_FAMILY (c6g, t4g, r6g, m6g) and GRAVITON_ALLOWED_FRAMEWORKS (pytorch, tensorflow).
- src/sagemaker/image_uris.py: private helper _get_image_scope_from_instance_type resolves the effective scope before config loading; "-sagemaker" suffix applied when the repo ends with "-inference-graviton"; fw_utils imported as a module to avoid the circular-import failure.
- pytorch.json / tensorflow.json: new inference_graviton section (aliases 1.12->1.12.1 and 2.9->2.9.1, py38, cpu, ubuntu20.04, 26 registries). Additions only.
- Tests: tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris/test_graviton.py (test_graviton_pytorch, test_graviton_tensorflow), graviton_framework_uri in expected_uris.py, and two module-scoped fixtures in tests/conftest.py.

Verification:
- Import orders (fw_utils, image_uris, package) succeed in fresh interpreters.
- Both new tests pass.
- Targeted run (image_uris, test_pytorch, tensorflow, training_compiler, test_fw_utils): 3225 passed, 2927 skipped, 0 failed.
- Manual checks of spec acceptance cases match.

Caveats:
- The shared venv lacks the mock package. I used a test-only shim in /tmp/gv_shim on PYTHONPATH for that run; the venv was not modified.
- Running without PYTHONPATH=src picks up a different checkout (base/src), so all runs used PYTHONPATH=src.
- No full unit-tree run and no clean before/after baseline (the first baseline was killed).

Choices: EIA requests keep the EIA scope (existing accelerator rule overrides); training requests on Graviton families now return the Graviton image, per spec.
